missionPremise: CTX-HAYS-REBIND (#653, merged c43e2436) added cad_property.quick_ref_id and property_number in migration 0099 and nothing populates them, because upsertCadProperties builds a WHOLE row. The rebind lane's own addendum (_inbox/2026-09-10_ctx-hays-rebind_addendum_source_reconciliation.json) measured what running the 8-26-2026 export through the existing cad-ingest CLI would cost: 45,524 of 134,216 Hays market values changed, about 5.8 billion dollars of absolute movement, source_file overwritten on every touched row. Identity columns and valuation columns have different blast radii and must not ride the same write. Which drop should be Hays' declared 2026 roll is an OPEN OPERATOR QUESTION and this lane does not answer it.
completionPredicate: A stranger can, without me: (1) check out feat/ctx-hays-backfill-published-identifiers and run `pnpm --filter @workspace/cad-ingest exec vitest run src/__tests__/publishedIdentifierBackfill.test.ts` and see 48 tests pass, every refusal asserted by rule name; (2) run the CLI with --dry-run against production read-only and see roll 134,606 / matched 134,216 / skipped-no-roll-row 375 / not-in-export 390; (3) run it with --dry-run against f06-staging-neondb and see it REFUSE with rule target-columns naming migration 0099; (4) hand it the IMPROVEMENT member and see it refuse by name; (5) add a column to BACKFILL_WRITABLE_COLUMNS and see the run refuse before issuing a statement. If any of those five does something else, this close is wrong.
scopeBasis: legacy-design-tools only, per the dispatch. The tool is BUILT and HANDED BACK; it has not been run against any store, because the integration seat owns execution and staging goes first. The re-derivation stops at the boundary of this lane's credentials: neondb is in scope, the atoms store (HAUSKA_MCP_DATABASE_URL) is not, which is why two of the five figures the dispatch listed could not be re-derived and are reported as not-re-derivable rather than agreed with. No tier gate was added to the declared-vintage refusal, deliberately: identity columns describe the account rather than the drop, so refusing on tier would be a control broader than its claim.

theMemberDiscriminationRule.problem: every member of a Hays drop is named PropertyDataExport<n>.txt, the numbering is not mnemonic, and extractCadDrop flattens to basenames so even the enclosing zip's name is gone by the time a reader sees the file. All six members share their first four columns (RecordType, PropertyID, QuickRefID, PropertyNumber), so a check for the identifier columns passes on every one of them. That is how the integration seat previously read the IMPROVEMENT member (103,490 rows) believing it was the roll (134,592).
theMemberDiscriminationRule.decision: BEAT header width rather than take it. Width is recorded in the durable record and is NOT the gate.
theMemberDiscriminationRule.whyNotWidth: width uniquely identifies PROPERTY (40) among these six, but OWNER, LAND and SEGMENT are ALL 21 columns, so it cannot name the sibling it refused; and an equality on 40 would refuse a valid future drop that adds a column, which is a refusal for a reason unrelated to the file's meaning.

rules.R1 identifier-columns-present: propertyid + quickrefid + propertynumber. NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. Kept only so a non-Orion file fails with the right message; its insufficiency is the documented reason R2 and R3 exist.
rules.R2 sibling-marker-absent: refuse when a column that positively identifies a sibling is present, and NAME the sibling. actyrbuilt -> SEGMENT, instanceid -> IMPROVEMENT, ownername/fullname -> OWNER, landtype -> LAND, saledate -> SALES. Order matters: SEGMENT and IMPROVEMENT both carry instanceid and only SEGMENT carries actyrbuilt.
rules.R3 property-columns-present: legaldesc + situs + marketvalue + squarefootage + legalacres. No sibling in a Hays drop carries any of these.
rules.R4 account-cardinality: duplicate PropertyID rows at most 0.1 percent of rows read, and it reads ROWS rather than the header. DECLARES ITSELF NOT APPLICABLE below 100 rows rather than firing on arithmetic noise, and says so in the durable record.

theMemberDiscriminationRule.whyR4IsTheMeaningShapedHalf: R1-R3 all read one payload's header, which is internal consistency: a single malformed header satisfies all three. R4 reads the body. Header and body are produced by different parts of the publisher's export job, so no single bad header can satisfy the whole gate.
howItWasTested: unit: the four SHARED columns alone pass R1 and the file is still refused (R3). The trap stated as a test.
unit: IMPROVEMENT, SEGMENT, OWNER, LAND and SALES headers each refused by R2 with identifiedAs set to the right member.
unit: a PROPERTY header with an EXTRA column is still ACCEPTED, which is what says width is not the gate.
unit, file-level: the IMPROVEMENT fixture and the pre-existing hays_owner / hays_land / hays_segment fixtures each refused by name through readPublishedIdentifiers.

unit: a 200-row PROPERTY-SHAPED file with four rows per account passes R1-R3 on its header and is refused by R4. Not vacuous: the real PROPERTY member is 0.00074 percent duplicates against a 0.1 percent ceiling, three orders of magnitude clear, and the improvement member is 5.2 percent.

theFindingThatMatteredMost.what: CP1 called the untouched-columns digest the money control and claimed no single party could satisfy both sides of it. That was WRONG.
theFindingThatMatteredMost.mechanism: the digest built its column list from information_schema MINUS BACKFILL_WRITABLE_COLUMNS. Adding market_value to that allowlist and to the SET clause is ONE conceptual edit, and it both moved a dollar on every row and removed market_value from the digest, which then reported VERIFIED. The list came from the catalog; the SUBTRACTION came from the thing being checked.
theFindingThatMatteredMost.howItWasFound: by MUTATING the writer and re-running the controls. Not by reading the code -- the code reads correctly. 'Enumerate from the catalog, exclude what we write, digest the rest' is the sentence you would write down as the right design.
theFindingThatMatteredMost.fix: DIGEST_EXCLUDED_COLUMNS stated independently; assertDigestScopeIntact() refusing on divergence in either direction; DIGEST_MUST_COVER as a positive list of money columns the digest must be watching.
bothLayersProvenByTheirOwnMutation: widen the writer's allowlist only -> REFUSED before any write, rule digest-scope, message names both sets
widen the allowlist AND DIGEST_EXCLUDED_COLUMNS so the first assertion agrees -> REFUSED before any write, rule digest-scope, 'the digest would not be watching market_value'
theFindingThatMatteredMost.honestResidual: two deliberate edits in two named places still get past both. Nothing survives an author trying to defeat it. What it now survives is the realistic failure: one edit that widens the writer and quietly blinds the check.

fleetMemory.text: A CHECKER WHOSE EXCLUSION SET IS DERIVED FROM THE THING IT CHECKS IS INTERNAL CONSISTENCY WEARING A MEANING-SHAPED COSTUME. My untouched-columns digest read its column list from information_schema (a genuinely independent source) and then subtracted the WRITER'S OWN ALLOWLIST. Widening the writer therefore widened the blind spot in the same edit, and the digest reported VERIFIED over a run that moved market_value on every row. The catalog half was independent; the subtraction half was not, and the subtraction is where the defect lived. When judging whether a check is meaning-shaped, check BOTH of its inputs, including the one that looks like a parameter rather than a source.

MUTATION IS THE ONLY THING THAT FOUND IT. I read that digest code three times and it reads correctly: 'enumerate from the catalog, exclude what we write, digest the rest' is the sentence you would write down as the right design. It took editing the writer to move a dollar and re-running the controls. For any control claimed to protect something valuable, break the protected thing on purpose and confirm the control fires. Reading the conclusion again is not a verification.

IN THIS ENVIRONMENT `python - <<'PY'` DOES NOT DELIVER A DOUBLED BACKSLASH VERBATIM: a `\\n` in the heredoc arrives at Python as a real newline. Every string patch anchored on a TypeScript template literal containing an escaped newline silently fails to match, and a patch script that asserts-and-exits leaves the file UNCHANGED while the test output that follows reads as a pass. Build the escape with chr(92) and anchor by line index, or use the Write tool. This cost me a false 'ALL CHECKS PASSED' that I nearly recorded.

A CONVENIENT RESULT IS A REASON TO DISTRUST THE INSTRUMENT. The first mutation run reported every check passing, which was the answer that would have been most comfortable, and it was produced by a mutation that never landed. One grep of the file changed the answer completely. Cost: ten seconds.

GENERATING A TEST FIXTURE CAN OVERWRITE A TRACKED ONE. I wrote hays_property_sample.txt, which orion.test.ts already uses, while generating my own samples. `git status` caught it before any commit. When scripting fixture generation into an existing __fixtures__ directory, list the directory first or namespace the filename.

A RATIO-BASED GATE NEEDS A DECLARED APPLICABILITY FLOOR OR IT FIRES ON TINY FIXTURES. My duplicate-ratio rule (0.1 percent ceiling) is right for a 134,592-row roll and meaningless on a 9-row fixture where one duplicate is 11 percent. The fix is not to weaken the ceiling: it is to declare the rule NOT APPLICABLE below a floor and say so in the output, which is the declared-degradation rule. A rule that silently skips itself on small inputs is the starved class.

AN UPDATE ... FROM (VALUES ...) MAKES 'NEVER INSERT' STRUCTURAL. There is no branch to forget and no check to go missing: the statement type cannot create a row. Where a constraint can be carried by the shape of the thing rather than by a guard around it, carry it there and let the test document the property rather than enforce it.

commits.subject: feat(P-124/CTX-HAYS-BACKFILL): write two identifier columns and nothing else, and the check that proves it was blind until a mutation run said so
fix(P-124/CTX-HAYS-BACKFILL): refuse a store where migration 0099 is not applied, because staging is one
test(P-124/CTX-HAYS-BACKFILL): violate the record-writer precondition instead of asserting it
fix(P-124/CTX-HAYS-BACKFILL): one transaction, so the digest PREVENTS a bad write instead of reporting one
fix(P-124/CTX-HAYS-BACKFILL): record a FAILED rollback instead of letting it replace the error

theTransaction.why: the dispatch asked that a run be PROVABLY UNABLE to alter a market value. What the first commit shipped was provably able to TELL YOU it had altered one: the untouched-columns digest runs after the batches, so a mismatch left the run committed and raised afterwards. For a money column that is a report, not a control.
theTransaction.what: the whole run is one transaction on one pg.Client. BEGIN, SET LOCAL statement_timeout='900s', digest-before, batches, digest-after; a mismatch throws, the catch ROLLBACKs, and nothing this tool wrote survives. A Pool would have spread the run across connections and made BEGIN meaningless.
theTransaction.sideEffect: the partial-run state is gone. 135 separate statements could fail at 130 and leave a county two-thirds written; one transaction either lands or does not, and the operation is idempotent so re-running after a rollback costs nothing.
theTransaction.theRollbackIsRecorded: a `rolled-back` line naming the reason and stating that every prop_id in the batch lines above was undone. A refusal that leaves no name is how an unattributed mutation becomes unanswerable.

verifiedBothDirectionsThroughTheRealCLI.forcedDigestMismatch: BEGIN, 4 rows updated, violation entry, ROLLBACK, and the table left with 0 of 5 rows carrying either identifier
verifiedBothDirectionsThroughTheRealCLI.cleanRun: BEGIN, 4 matched, 4 updated, VERIFIED unchanged over 21 columns, COMMIT, and the table carrying the identifiers with 0 empty strings, 1 honest NULL quick_ref_id, 2 honest NULL property_number, and one distinct market_value

theTransaction.howTheMismatchWasForced: a SCRATCH mutation appending a suffix to the after-digest, applied and reverted, never committed. The digest logic itself was not changed.
theTransaction.failedRollbackIsRecordedToo: if ROLLBACK itself throws, its error used to REPLACE the original refusal and the rolled-back line was never written, so the record ended at run-end and a reader could take that for a commit. Absent and failed looked the same, in the record of a tool built to stop exactly that. The rollback now runs in its own try and both outcomes are recorded; a failed one says plainly that the server aborting an open transaction on a dead connection is an INFERENCE, not an observation.

scopeOfTheClaims.whatProvablyUnableToAlterAMarketValueMEA: the UPDATE's WHERE pins county_fips and tax_year, so the statement structurally cannot reach a row outside the county-year it was given; the digest is scoped to that SAME county-year; and the whole run is one transaction that rolls back on a digest mismatch. Inside that scope the claim is earned. Outside it the tool cannot reach, so there is nothing to claim.
scopeOfTheClaims.whatItDoesNotDo: it never CREATES an empty-string identifier -- textOrNull turns a published blank into null at read time and COALESCE leaves the cell alone -- but it does not CLEAN UP an empty string that predates it. On production that population is zero today (0 non-null quick_ref_id and 0 non-null property_number at 48209/2026), so the distinction is currently theoretical. Stated because a later reader should not infer a repair the tool does not perform.
scopeOfTheClaims.theDigestIsScopedNotGlobal: it digests cad_property at (county_fips, declared tax_year), not the whole table. A write to another county during the run is neither detected nor rolled back, and is also not something this tool can cause. Naming the exclusion because an instrument's exclusion set is part of its contract.

diffShape.read: PURELY ADDITIVE. Not one line of existing code changed; the only edit to a pre-existing file is a single script line in lib/cad-ingest/package.json. upsertCadProperties, the Orion parser, the vintage resolver and every existing caller are untouched, so this writer cannot regress the ingest path. It also means the only way this ships a defect is through code nothing calls yet, which is why the verification is weighted toward running the tool rather than reading it.
